items.title: Deutsche Bank, PNB ink pact to fund M&As
items.description: Deutsche Bank and Punjab National Bank have signed a preliminary agreement to finance corporate acquisitions in India. This partnership follows recent reforms that allow domestic lenders to fund up to 75% of corporate deal values. State Bank of India has also entered a similar partnership with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group. The agreement aims to support Indian companies in their growth and strategic expansion efforts.

items.title: These mid-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%, according to analysts
items.description: There is a new worry for the market, and it is best to be prepared for it. After almost six months, the threat of US tariffs is back. Tariff talk is exactly the kind of thing that impacts sentiment without touching the fundamentals of companies.

items.title: India's net FDI outflows widen to $4.95 billion in September
items.description: India's foreign direct investment landscape saw a net outflow of $4.95 billion in September, markedly higher than last year. In the same month, gross inflows decreased by 17.6%, totaling $5.91 billion, impacted by a rise in repatriation and disinvestment. Indian firms invested $4.41 billion abroad. Yet, from April to September, net FDI inflows surged, with total gross inflows up by 15.5% to $60.91 billion.

items.title: Gujarat overtakes Maharashtra as India's top state for active investors
items.description: Gujarat has become the state with the highest number of active investors, surpassing Maharashtra. The data indicates a significant increase in the number of active investors in recent months. Active investors in Maharashtra also increased, but not as much as in Gujarat. Additionally, Uttar Pradesh remains in third place, showing growth in its investor count. The total active unique investors in India reached a two-year high in October.

items.title: Indian stocks defy Asia rout, hit fresh FY27 highs on global fund rotation
items.description: India's equity indices saw a notable increase as they defied trends in the Asia-Pacific region. Investor confidence was bolstered by resilient domestic corporate earnings and decreased focus on AI stocks. Key contributors to this rise included ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and Reliance Industries. Meanwhile, foreign funds recorded significant investments in Indian equities, marking a shift in market dynamics. Overall, Indian markets remained comparatively stable despite fluctuating conditions in Asian markets.

items.title: D-Street poised for a positive start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
items.description: Markets experienced a significant rebound, recovering nearly 2% from Monday's sell-off, indicating strong underlying buying interest. Analysts suggest that despite the recovery, some consolidation may be necessary in the near term. Foreign portfolio investors net bought shares worth Rs 4,479 crore, while domestic investors were net sellers at Rs 4,019 crore. The Indian rupee rose to its highest level this financial year due to strong foreign inflows.

items.title: Stocks in news: LG Electronics, HDFC Bank, Siemens Energy, Lupin and Schaeffler India
items.description: Domestic equities rebounded strongly as the Nifty 50 surged by 470 points post-market holiday. Major players like LG Electronics India and HDFC Bank made headlines with noteworthy updates, reigniting investor enthusiasm. Waaree Renewable Technologies received a favorable assessment from CARE Ratings, improving its financial outlook. Additionally, Siemens Energy showcased impressive quarterly earnings, reflecting strong growth in both revenue and profit margins.

items.title: Retail investors turn net sellers in November as FIIs pile into Indian stocks
items.description: In November, retail investors, mutual funds, and insurance companies sold significant amounts of Indian growth assets. Retail investors experienced their largest selling in history, totaling around ₹24,953 crore. This marks the second consecutive month of outflows from retail investors. Additionally, mutual funds reported their first monthly net selling since August 2022, amounting to ₹34,929 crore. Despite the selling trend, retail investors have maintained a net buying position in 2026.

items.title: Gold crash triggers auction notices as LTV breaches hit lenders
items.description: Gold finance companies are issuing legal auction notices due to breaches in loan-to-value limits amid falling gold prices. This trend has been driven by a significant decline in gold prices over the past weeks. Nearly 40% of gold-loan portfolios have seen their loan-to-value ratios exceed permissible levels. Lenders are encouraging borrowers to provide additional collateral or make partial payments to avoid auctions.

items.title: Govt mulls special shares to retain control of merged PFC-REC entity
items.description: In a strategic move, the Centre is planning a capital structure featuring special shares to facilitate the PFC-REC merger, ensuring majority voting control. To finance this initiative, the government is expected to allocate around Rs 7,500-8,000 crore despite holding a lower share post-merger. The plan will also include issuing shares with ordinary and enhanced voting rights, subject to Cabinet approval for the proposed funding.

items.title: Stock Radar: Union Bank of India stock hit a fresh record high in November 2026; time to buy or book profits?
items.description: Union Bank of India reached a fresh record high following a breakout from an inverse head and shoulders pattern. The stock has noted significant gains, increasing by over 19% in the last month alone. Trading volumes have surged, demonstrating strong buying participation from market participants. Traders are advised to maintain a positive outlook with a potential target of 255 to 290 levels.

items.title: PSBs may find it hard to keep lending pace as liquidity tightens
items.description: Public sector banks could struggle to sustain aggressive loan growth amid diminishing liquidity advantages and growing deposit challenges. The loan-to-deposit ratios of public and private sector banks have shown significant narrowing recently. Private sector banks' deposit growth outpaced that of public sector banks, impacting their competitive edge. State-owned banks have expressed optimism about liquidity positions while acknowledging potential pressure on deposit rates.

items.title: Inflation pressures broaden across India, raising rate-hike risks ahead of RBI's December review
items.description: Inflationary pressures spread across goods, services and regions in October, with a larger share of items breaching the 4% threshold, the RBI's November bulletin showed. Retail inflation climbed to 6.09%, crossing the central bank's upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years, potentially complicating its December monetary policy decision.

items.title: Noel Tata-led trust gets nod to invest Rs 150 crore in financially sound companies
items.description: Maharashtra charity commissioner has granted permission to Tata Social Welfare Trust for new investment opportunities. The trust can now invest ₹150 crore in shares of financially stable and well-governed companies. This expansion includes investments through a dedicated vehicle monitored by an investment committee. The trust plans to regularly assess investments while ensuring compliance with all necessary regulations. Qualified advisers will assist in overseeing investment decisions, enhancing the fund’s strategic management.
